text:
maria: Heads-up: our Python SDK sample app failing on Windows 3.11 with SSL verify error when running the quickstart. Anyone seen this?

devon: I ran into something similar last week. What's the traceback?

maria: Here's the relevant piece from the failing run:
```
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1129)
  File "site-packages/redwood_sdk/http.py", line 128, in request
    resp = await self._session.request(...)
```
Repro steps: Windows 11, Python 3.11.4, venv, pip install redwood-sdk (no certifi), run sample app that calls Streaming API. Works fine on mac/linux.

sam: On Windows the stdlib cert store behaves differently depending on Python build. On mac/linux OpenSSL/certifi covers most cases. Do you have certifi installed?

maria: No certifi in that environment.

devon: Our SDK currently tries: 1) SSL_CERT_FILE env var 2) certifi.where() 3) fallback. I think the fallback path ends up calling `load_verify_locations(None)` which is unreliable on Windows builds that don't ship an OpenSSL cert bundle. We expected `ssl.create_default_context()` to pick up the platform store but that doesn't always happen when we override contexts for connection pooling.

jess: I opened GH issue #2043 with stack and a minimal repro (attached). Suggestion: change SDK to prefer `create_default_context()` and only call `load_verify_locations` with explicit files if env or certifi is present. Also add clearer docs about Windows caveats.

maria: Also seeing a weird async hang when using the async client on Python 3.12: stream yields first chunk then stalls indefinitely on ProactorEventLoop. Could be related to how we offload TLS handshake or how token refresh is done.

sam: Windows 3.8-3.12 have different default event loop semantics. uvloop isn't available on Windows so small differences matter. Check for code that does `loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()` vs `get_running_loop()`; the former can be problematic on ProactorEventLoop.

devon: FYI there is also an auth edge: token refresh path makes a synchronous HTTP call in the auth library which blocks the event loop on Windows in some builds. That can look like a hang when streaming and a token expires mid-stream. I have a PR draft to make token refresh fully async.

ci-bot: Created branch `fix/windows-ssl-cert-fallback` and pushed tests to CI matrix (windows-3.11, windows-3.12, ubuntu-3.11). Added a unit test that simulates missing certifi and ensures we still construct a usable SSLContext.

jess: Short-term workaround for users: `pip install certifi` or set `SSL_CERT_FILE` to `python -c "import certifi; print(certifi.where())"`. I'll add that to the quickstart and troubleshooting docs.

maria: Can the SDK emit a RuntimeWarning or more helpful error message suggesting `pip install certifi` and `SSL_CERT_FILE` if verification fails on Windows? It's a common onboarding friction.

devon: Agreed. We can augment the exception handler to detect `SSLCertVerificationError` and include a hint. Also add telemetry event so we can see how often this hits new signups.

sam: Separately, typing/compat issue: mypy on 3.8 flags a bunch of AsyncClient methods due to missing back-compat stubs. We should add `typing_extensions` extras and inline overloads for py<3.9. I'll file a follow-up PR for typing fixes and small runtime guards for asyncio APIs.

jess: For the GH issue I recommended three deliverables: 1) change SSLContext fallback logic, 2) async token refresh fix, 3) quickstart doc update + warning.

maria: Thanks — leaving the repro and logs in the GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2043 

devon: I'll shepherd the SSL fix; sam's on typing/async. CI will run the Windows matrix to validate.

maria: Awesome. If anyone hits this in the wild, ping here and we can triage. :thumbsup:
